label: Complexes of Groups
notes: Open by recalling Bass-Serre theory: a group acting on a tree is encoded by a graph of groups. This chapter, printed pages 519 to 572, asks for the higher-dimensional analogue, where the quotient is a polyhedral complex rather than a graph and the bookkeeping needs Haefliger's scwol language.

label: From Graphs of Groups
notes: Stress what survives and what breaks. A graph of groups always develops to a tree; that is the miracle of dimension one. In higher dimensions an arbitrary complex of groups need not develop at all, so developability becomes a theorem to be earned rather than a free gift.

label: Small Categories Without Loops
notes: Define a scwol carefully. Vertices carry a dimension grading; non-identity arrows strictly decrease it, so there are no non-trivial loops and no non-trivial automorphisms of an object. The barycentric subdivision of any polyhedral complex is the canonical example feeding the whole construction.

label: Complex of Groups Over a Scwol
notes: Walk through the three pieces of data: local groups on objects, injective twisting homomorphisms along arrows, and elements correcting composition. Emphasize that the correction elements are not optional decoration; they record the failure of strict functoriality and carry genuine cohomological content.

label: The Cocycle Condition
notes: Explain that the twisting elements must satisfy a compatibility identity over every composable pair of arrows. This is a non-abelian two-cocycle condition. When the local groups are abelian it literally lives in degree-two cohomology, which is the obstruction theory students should keep in the back of their minds.

label: Fundamental Group
notes: Build the fundamental group as a quotient of the free product of local groups with the edge generators, modulo relations from the twisting data and a chosen spanning tree. This generalizes the fundamental group of a graph of groups and reduces to it exactly when the scwol is one-dimensional.

label: The Universal Development
notes: Describe the development as the space the fundamental group acts on, assembled from cosets of local groups glued by the connecting maps. When it exists it is simply connected and its quotient recovers the original scwol, exactly mirroring how the Bass-Serre tree sits over a graph of groups.

label: Developability
notes: Define developable precisely: the complex of groups arises from a genuine action on a simply connected scwol. Equivalently every local group injects into the fundamental group. Warn that this can fail; give the intuition that obstructions are local linking-condition failures detected one vertex at a time.

label: The Local Development
notes: Introduce the local development at a vertex as the model link the universal object must exhibit there. It is always defined even when the global development is not, which is why curvature, a purely local condition, can be checked on it without first knowing developability holds.

label: Non-Positive Curvature Theorem
notes: State Haefliger's theorem: if every local development is CAT(0), or more generally CAT(kappa) locally with the link condition, then the complex of groups is developable and the development is CAT(0). This is the higher-dimensional Cartan-Hadamard mechanism transplanted into the combinatorial setting.

label: Constructing Groups
notes: Show the payoff direction. Prescribe local groups and gluing on a complex whose shapes force large links, verify the metric link condition combinatorially, and the theorem hands back a group acting properly cocompactly on a CAT(0) space, with the local data realized as actual stabilizers.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: Close by tying the four invariants together: scwol, complex of groups, fundamental group, development. Remind students that local non-positive curvature is the bridge from combinatorial data to a global simply connected geometry, and point ahead to applications in Coxeter and right-angled group constructions.
